title: Covariate Copies Count as Evidence in Time-Series Foundation Models (Zenodo, v1)
note: Version 1 record (the scan's primary URL). The fetch returned the description but no page header; date and version come from the API record. Abstract: eight copies of a covariate raise its implied weight in Chronos-2, t0-beta and TiRex-2; on GEFCom2012 and 2017 four temperature copies multiply WQL by 0.878 to 1.018; a source bias returns the one-temperature forecast.

title: Zenodo API record 23003932
note: API record of version 1: preprint, publication date 2026-09-28, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23003932, concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23003931, flagged as not the latest version. The only file is the manuscript PDF (copy-evidence-v1.pdf); no code, data or results files attached. Two authors (National Tsing Hua University, EchoBoost AI).

title: Covariate Copies Count as Evidence in Time-Series Foundation Models (Zenodo, v2)
note: Version 2, a non-peer-reviewed preprint, PDF only. Adds 18 fev-bench tasks (every dynamic covariate supplied eight times raises error in three of four models) and a day-ahead pipeline test on an energy dataset with a duplicated weather station. Replaces the v1 comparison of corrections and states that copies sometimes improve accuracy, which declaring a source gives up.

title: Covariate Copies Count as Evidence in Time-Series Foundation Models (Zenodo, v5)
note: Version 5, latest fetched; PDF only. Corrects the t0-beta results (now run with the model's known-future attention mask); headline unchanged: eight copies raise the implied log evidence ratio by 0.81, 0.71 and 2.28 nats (Chronos-2, t0-beta, TiRex-2). Now says averaging channels beats the source bias in point estimate on correlated measurements and the bias is not consistently better on loss.

title: copy-evidence-v5.pdf: GEFCom protocol (Appendix F)
note: GEFCom protocol: fev-bench tasks proenfo_gfc12 (11 load series) and proenfo_gfc17 (8 ISO-NE zones) at a pinned revision with file hashes. Horizon 168 hours, weekly cutoffs, 10 windows for GEFCom2012 and 20 for GEFCom2017, context 2,048 hours. Temperature enters as a known-future covariate with actual values (oracle weather). Arms: one temperature, four copies, unit aliases, all temperatures.

title: copy-evidence-v5.pdf: Table 4, four temperature copies vs one
note: Table 4, WQL ratio of four temperature copies to one, 95% bootstrap intervals over windows. Chronos-2: 0.997 [0.976, 1.018] on GEFCom2012, 1.018 [0.999, 1.037] on GEFCom2017. t0-beta: 1.009 [0.984, 1.039] and 0.931 [0.895, 0.964]. TiRex-2: 0.928 [0.855, 0.994] and 0.878 [0.825, 0.931]. Intervals exclude 1 in 3 of 6 pairs, all improvements; both Chronos-2 intervals include 1.

title: copy-evidence-v5.pdf: source bias on GEFCom (sections 5.3 and 6)
note: With the training-free source bias (minus log 4 on the copies' attention keys), four temperature copies give the one-temperature forecast to within 4.6e-6 of the interval width on all GEFCom windows. That also gives up any gain from copies: WQL relative to uncorrected copies rises by up to a factor of 1.140 (TiRex-2, GEFCom2017). The bias needs a change inside the model's variate attention.

title: copy-evidence-v5.pdf: day-ahead pipeline test (section 5.2)
note: GEFCom2017 / ISO-NE: zones RI and SEMASS carry an identical temperature series (one station, Providence, in the source workbook). In a constructed day-ahead test (24 h, eight zones) repeated temperature inputs change forecasts of all three models; mean log-WQL difference -0.064 to -0.007, lower loss for the repeated input in 12 of 12 cells, intervals excluding zero in 11.

title: copy-evidence-v5.pdf: models, code, limitations
note: Weights pinned: amazon/chronos-2 at 29ec3766 (chronos-forecasting 2.3.2), theforecastingcompany/t0-beta at c8885416 with a patched tfc-t0 0.5.0, NX-AI/TiRex-2 at 05e5b26d; CPU, fp32. Code: on request from the corresponding author only. Limitations stated: oracle weather; pretraining corpora may include GEFCom. One synthetic comparison had its statistics fixed before results; no registry named.
